sources.description: Requirements 3.1-3.10 define identity, tool-cluster, weak-signal, exclusion, and canonical taxonomy behavior.
Requirements 12.1-12.3 require evidence-backed harness positives and ordinary technical-chat/Cline negatives.
Shared identity matching is bounded and exact; generic SDK identities are not coding-agent identities.
Rule A evidence codes and the high-confidence identity boundary.
Rule B requires canonical file read/search, local mutation, and OS-command categories.
Rule C requires read/search plus local mutation and a recognized project marker; .git alone is not decisive.
The stock heuristic ignores weak technical, model, web, one-tool, and generic SDK signals.
Identity exclusions apply prospectively and never downgrade an established positive.
The acceptance matrix reuses root matcher, tool classification, compaction, and explicit-completion research.
Current Codex source defines the codex_cli_rs originator used by its client User-Agent.
Current Codex source builds the versioned codex_cli_rs User-Agent.
Current Codex source inserts the constructed value into the HTTP User-Agent header.
Current Roo OpenAI-native provider emits a versioned roo-code User-Agent.
The root compatibility tests positively match opencode/1.2.26 from extension.agent; classification fixtures pass the proven token through the accepted ClientUserAgent field.
The root OpenCode matcher reads bounded agent identity candidates.
The root compatibility tests positively match the Pi value from extension.user_agent; classification fixtures pass the proven token through the accepted ClientUserAgent field.
The root Pi matcher recognizes bounded stable identity markers.
The root Droid matcher recognizes Factory CLI identity tokens from agent candidates; classification fixtures pass the proven token through the accepted ClientUserAgent field.
A Droid-like tool list alone is not enough for the existing root matcher.
The root compatibility tests positively match hermes-agent/1.0 NousResearch from extension.agent; classification fixtures pass the proven token through the accepted ClientUserAgent field.
The root Hermes matcher recognizes bounded stable identity markers.
Cline may expose underlying Anthropic/JS or OpenAI/JS identities rather than a stable Cline-specific User-Agent.
Cline discussion documenting inconsistent and SDK-like User-Agent behavior.
The archived survey records cross-harness tool names and aliases that informed canonical tool classification.
ClassifyToolName owns the exact name-to-category mapping and ignores descriptions and arguments.
Cline and Roo use attempt_completion as a completion signal; this alone is not a client identity rule.
The compaction survey records prompt/summary signatures, including Aider, which are outside session identity evidence.

harnessIdentitySupport.reason: Current Codex source emits a versioned codex_cli_rs identity, so the family token is supported as a high-confidence client identity.
Current Roo source emits a versioned roo-code identity on relevant OpenAI and Codex traffic.
The root matcher proves this stable identity from extension.agent. The classification fixture uses the same value in the accepted user_agent input field.
The root matcher proves this stable identity from extension.user_agent. The classification fixture uses the same value in the accepted user_agent input field.
The root matcher accepts the distinctive factory-cli identity and rejects a Droid-like tool list without identity evidence. The classification fixture uses the accepted user_agent input field.
The root matcher proves this stable identity from extension.agent. The classification fixture uses the same value in the accepted user_agent input field.
These SDK-like identities are shared and do not establish that the client is Cline; each remains unknown without independent decisive evidence.
The surveyed Aider evidence is a prompt/summary compaction signature, not a supported stable User-Agent identity. V1 does not inspect those prompt signatures, so User-Agent alone is unsupported.

fixtures.reason: The versioned Codex User-Agent is a supported high-confidence identity and is independently sufficient.
The versioned Roo User-Agent is a supported high-confidence identity and is independently sufficient.
The existing root matcher fixture demonstrates this stable agent identity; the source field is recorded explicitly for later canonicalization.
The existing root matcher fixture demonstrates a stable Pi User-Agent identity.
The distinctive factory-cli agent identity is supported; this positive does not rely on the Droid tool list alone.
The existing root matcher fixture demonstrates a stable Hermes identity.
Anthropic/JS is an underlying SDK identity shared by clients and cannot identify Cline by itself.
OpenAI/JS is a generic underlying SDK identity and cannot identify Cline by itself.
The generic SDK identity remains non-evidence, while the current turn's canonical read, search, edit, and OS-command categories form the independent decisive cluster.
A missing User-Agent does not block an independently decisive canonical tool cluster.
Read/search plus one local mutation lacks both the OS-command category required by Rule B and the project marker required by Rule C.
Generic .git is explicitly not a decisive project marker, so read plus edit remains weak evidence.
Canonical read/search and mutation categories are corroborated by the recognized Go project marker go.mod.
A lone generic shell tool does not form a distinctive coding-tool cluster.
A web lookup tool alone is not coding-agent evidence.
One file-read category without search, mutation, command, identity, or marker evidence remains unknown.
One file-search category without other decisive evidence remains unknown.
